![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14259215/assets/c5e5d3d52788c982a25e8c373346c14e47cd9481ef34c72ea87f8f8562888432.png)

Given the triangle above, find the length of $\overset{―}{AB}$ rounded to one decimal place.
question.worked_solution:
For an angle $\theta $ in a right triangle, the trigonometric ratios are as follows:

- $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{opposite leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$

- $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{adjacent leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$

- $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{opposite leg}}{\text{adjacent leg}}$

First, note that we are given the length of the adjacent $\overset{―}{BC}$ and wish to find the length of the leg $\overset{―}{AB}$ hypotenuse to the given angle $∠B.$

The trigonometric ratio that relates the adjacent leg to the hypotenuse is *cosine*. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(m∠C) & =\frac{\text{adjacent leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡({36}^{∘}) & =\frac{7.28}{AC} \\ AC\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡({36}^{∘}) & =7.28 \\ AC & =\frac{7.28}{\operatorname{cos}⁡({36}^{∘})}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using a calculator to evaluate the trigonometric ratio, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}AC & =\frac{7.28}{\operatorname{cos}⁡({36}^{∘})} \\  & =\frac{7.28}{(0.809\,01…)} \\  & =8.998\,57… \\  & ≈9.0,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to one decimal place.
